lines.t: Today's special guest is Lord Blackwell, one of our country's most experienced and distinguished career diplomats.
lines.zh: 今天的特邀嘉宾是布莱克威尔勋爵，我国最有经验、最杰出的职业外交官之一。
cloze: Today's special guest is Lord Blackwell, one of our country's most experienced and
career diplomats.

lines.t: Welcome.
lines.zh: 欢迎。

lines.t: It's my pleasure.
lines.zh: 这是我的荣幸。

lines.t: Our audience will be most interested in learning about a career in the foreign service.
lines.zh: 我们的观众最感兴趣的是了解外交部门的职业生涯。

lines.t: However, before we talk about that, I'd like to ask you about the current developments hitting the news today regarding the Republic of Winopia.
lines.zh: 然而，在我们谈论这个之前，我想问一下今天新闻中有关维诺皮亚共和国的最新进展。
cloze: However, before we talk about that, I'd like to ask you about the current
hitting the news today regarding the Republic of Winopia.

lines.t: What can you tell us?
lines.zh: 你能告诉我们什么？

lines.t: I'm afraid I don't know much beyond what we've all seen on the news.
lines.zh: 除了我们在新闻上看到的以外，恐怕我不知道太多。

lines.t: It looks like the government of Winopia seems to be undergoing some sort of crisis of legitimacy and an interim administration has been transitionally established until a head of state is agreed on.
lines.zh: 看起来维诺皮亚政府似乎正在经历某种合法性危机，临时政府已经过渡成立，直到就国家元首达成一致。

lines.t: But my career work has mostly focused around the Continental spheres of Europe and the Americas, and thus I've never been involved with Winopian relations.
lines.zh: 但我的职业生涯主要集中在欧洲和美洲大陆领域，因此我从未参与过温诺普关系。
cloze: But my career work has mostly focused around the Continental spheres of Europe and the Americas, and thus I've never been involved with Winopian

lines.t: It's for this reason that I don't know anything on this matter beyond what we can all read in the newspapers.
lines.zh: 正因如此，除了我们在报纸上读到的信息外，我对此事一无所知。

lines.t: Oh, I see.
lines.zh: 我懂了。

lines.t: Nevertheless, be rest assured that our export envoys at our consulate there will be closely monitoring the situation and I expect our bilateral relations with that country will not be affected.
lines.zh: 尽管如此，请放心，我们驻该国领事馆的出口特使将密切关注事态发展，我希望我们与该国的双边关系不会受到影响。

lines.t: So how does one get a career in foreign relations?
lines.zh: 那么如何才能从事外交工作呢？
cloze: So how does one get a career in foreign

lines.t: There are many different paths one can take.
lines.zh: 人们可以采取许多不同的路径。

lines.t: All diplomats have their own story.
lines.zh: 所有外交官都有自己的故事。
cloze: All
have their own story.

lines.t: But in my case, I got a degree in electrical engineering followed by six years' service in the Air Force.
lines.zh: 但就我而言，我获得了电气工程学位，随后在空军服役了六年。

lines.t: Then I went to a law school and upon obtaining a degree in international law, I joined the diplomatic core where I've been for 22 years.
lines.zh: 然后我去了法学院，获得国际法学位后，我加入了外交核心，在那里我已经工作了 22 年。
cloze: Then I went to a law school and upon obtaining a degree in
law, I joined the diplomatic core where I've been for 22 years.

lines.t: What would you say are the key skills one needs for the job?
lines.zh: 您认为这项工作所需的关键技能是什么？

lines.t: There are so many.
lines.zh: 有这么多。

lines.t: Being a hard worker and good student is important—you never stop learning.
lines.zh: 努力工作和好学生很重要——你永远不会停止学习。

lines.t: In addition, a diplomat needs to be very articulate in their discourse and rhetoric.
lines.zh: 此外，外交官的话语和言辞必须非常清晰。
cloze: In addition, a diplomat needs to be very
in their discourse and rhetoric.

lines.t: Whether it is diffusing tension or enacting policy, people and communication skills are vital.
lines.zh: 无论是缓解紧张局势还是制定政策，人员和沟通技巧都至关重要。

lines.t: One thing I’ve learned in a quarter century of management is that there are ample gray areas in human behavior and that there may not always be clear right-or-wrong solutions to employee disputes.
lines.zh: 我在四分之一个世纪的管理生涯中学到的一件事是，人类行为中存在大量的灰色地带，并且对于员工纠纷可能并不总是有明确的正确或错误的解决方案。
cloze: One thing I’ve learned in a quarter century of management is that there are ample gray areas in human behavior and that there may not always be clear
solutions to employee disputes.

lines.t: When two people have different versions of the same event, it can be hard to know whom to believe.
lines.zh: 当两个人对同一事件有不同的版本时，很难知道该相信谁。

lines.t: One such circumstance always comes back to me.
lines.zh: 我总是会想起这样一种情况。
cloze: One such
always comes back to me.

lines.t: It happened years ago and it’s a measure of the forgettable nature of the conflict that I no longer even recall what the dispute was about, but I definitely recall the resolution.
lines.zh: 这件事发生在几年前，我什至不记得这场争端是关于什么的，但我绝对记得解决方案。

lines.t: Two talented young executives, one of whom I was managing, had vastly different accounts of the same event and it seemed likely we’d never get to the truth.
lines.zh: 两位才华横溢的年轻高管（其中一位是我所管理的）对同一事件的描述截然不同，我们似乎永远无法了解真相。
cloze: Two talented young
, one of whom I was managing, had vastly different accounts of the same event and it seemed likely we’d never get to the truth.

lines.t: We reached the deadlock.
lines.zh: 我们陷入了僵局。

lines.t: And the manager of the other individual said, “Here’s something I learned from an excellent manager I once worked for.
lines.zh: 另一个人的经理说：“这是我从我曾经工作过的一位优秀经理那里学到的东西。
cloze: And the manager of the other individual said, “Here’s something I learned from an
manager I once worked for.

lines.t: He used to say, ‘when in doubt, assume positive intent.’” And just like that, we had a path forward.
lines.zh: 他常说，‘当有疑问时，要抱有积极的意图。’”就这样，我们有了前进的道路。

lines.t: My counterpart and I agreed we might never ascertain the actual facts of the matter.
lines.zh: 我和我的对手一致认为，我们可能永远无法查明事情的真相。
cloze: My
and I agreed we might never ascertain the actual facts of the matter.

lines.t: Quite likely there were elements of truth in both employees' stories.
lines.zh: 两名员工的故事中很可能都有真实的成分。

lines.t: We agreed to monitor their actions and relationship going forward, but to intervene no further.
lines.zh: 我们同意监控他们未来的行动和关系，但不再进行干预。
cloze: We agreed to monitor their actions and
going forward, but to intervene no further.

lines.t: We assumed the best about both of them and moved on.
lines.zh: 我们对他们俩都抱有最好的看法，然后继续前进。

lines.t: The result was that we were able to put the conflict behind us.
lines.zh: 结果是我们能够把冲突抛在脑后。
cloze: The result was that we were able to put the
behind us.

lines.t: In fact, their problems didn't recur.
lines.zh: 事实上，他们的问题并没有再次出现。

lines.t: Over the years this general approach has proved useful.
lines.zh: 多年来，这种通用方法已被证明是有用的。
cloze: Over the years this general
has proved useful.

lines.t: Whenever the truth is obscure, assuming positive intent and agreeing to move on can be a constructive decision.
lines.zh: 当真相模糊不清时，表现出积极的意图并同意继续前进可能是一个建设性的决定。

lines.t: For some Americans, going out to dinner is a treat, planned and budgeted for.
lines.zh: 对于一些美国人来说，出去吃饭是一种享受，是有计划和预算的。
cloze: For some Americans, going out to dinner is a treat, planned and
for.

lines.t: For others, it's just a daily occurrence.
lines.zh: 对于其他人来说，这只是每天都会发生的事情。

lines.t: And that second group of people is becoming the majority, as the number of Americans who enjoy cooking is declining.
lines.zh: 随着喜欢烹饪的美国人数量不断减少，第二类人正在成为大多数。
cloze: And that second group of people is becoming the majority, as the number of Americans who enjoy cooking is

lines.t: In the early 2000s, researcher Eddie Yoon conducted a survey to ascertain Americans' attitudes to cooking.
lines.zh: 2000 年代初，研究员 Eddie Yoon 进行了一项调查，以确定美国人对烹饪的态度。

lines.t: The survey found that $15\%$ of Americans loved to cook, $50\%$ said they hated to cook and $35\%$ reported mixed feelings.
lines.zh: 调查发现，$15\%$ 的美国人喜欢做饭，$50\%$ 表示他们讨厌做饭，$35\%$ 则表示心情复杂。
cloze: The survey found that $15\%$ of Americans loved to cook, $50\%$ said they hated to cook and $35\%$
mixed feelings.

lines.t: When Yoon conducted the same survey 15 years later, only $10\%$ of respondents reported a love of cooking, $45\%$ said they hated it, and $45\%$ had mixed feelings.
lines.zh: 15 年后，当 Yoon 进行同样的调查时，只有 $10\%$ 的受访者表示热爱烹饪，$45\%$ 表示讨厌烹饪，而 $45\%$ 则心情复杂。

lines.t: Yoon asserts cooking is akin to sewing.
lines.zh: 尹声称烹饪类似于缝纫。
cloze: Yoon asserts cooking is akin to

lines.t: As recently as the early 20th century, many Americans sewed their own clothing.
lines.zh: 就在 20 世纪初，许多美国人还自己缝制衣服。

lines.t: Today, the vast majority of Americans buy clothing; only a tiny minority still sew and they do it mainly as a hobby.
lines.zh: 如今，绝大多数美国人购买服装；只有极少数人仍在缝纫，而且他们主要将其作为一种爱好。
cloze: Today, the vast majority of Americans buy clothing; only a tiny
still sew and they do it mainly as a hobby.

lines.t: Yoon believes the number of home cooks will diminish in a similar fashion.
lines.zh: 尹相信家庭厨师的数量也会以类似的方式减少。

lines.t: Currently, the average American household spends over $3,000 per year on dining out.
lines.zh: 目前，美国家庭平均每年外出就餐花费超过 3,000 美元。
cloze: Currently, the average American
spends over $3,000 per year on dining out.

lines.t: However, what people save in convenience, they lose in cash.
lines.zh: 然而，人们在方便时省下的钱，却损失了现金。

lines.t: Take buying lunch on work days, for example.
lines.zh: 以工作日购买午餐为例。
cloze: Take buying lunch on work days, for

lines.t: People spend on average $10 per meal when they buy lunch.
lines.zh: 人们购买午餐时平均每餐花费 10 美元。

lines.t: Making your own lunch, meanwhile, will cost less.
lines.zh: 同时，自己做午餐会花费更少。
cloze: Making your own lunch,
, will cost less.

lines.t: One survey found people only spend on average $6.30 when they bring lunch prepared at home.
lines.zh: 一项调查发现，人们携带在家准备的午餐时平均只花费 6.30 美元。

lines.t: Americans' growing aversion to spending time in the kitchen signifies a host of challenges for the grocery industry.
lines.zh: 美国人越来越不愿意花时间在厨房里，这意味着食品杂货行业面临着一系列挑战。
cloze: Americans' growing aversion to spending time in the kitchen signifies a host of

lines.t: Every year, of the more than 2.5 billion bags checked onto flights worldwide, 26 million go missing.
lines.zh: 每年，全球航班托运的超过 25 亿件行李中，有 2600 万件失踪。
cloze: Every year, of the more than 2.5 billion bags checked onto flights
, 26 million go missing.

lines.t: And of that 26 million, 1 million never make it back to their original owner.
lines.zh: 而在这 2600 万之中，有 100 万再也没有回到原来的主人身边。

lines.t: Bad weather and flight delays, miscoded destination tags, and some people simply forgetting to pick up one of their bags are a few of the reasons.
lines.zh: 恶劣天气和航班延误、目的地标签编码错误以及有些人只是忘记领取其中一个行李都是其中一些原因。
cloze: Bad weather and flight delays, miscoded
tags, and some people simply forgetting to pick up one of their bags are a few of the reasons.

lines.t: But the number one reason a bag ends up lost is that it has no ID tag and airlines don't know to whom it belongs.
lines.zh: 但行李最终丢失的首要原因是它没有身份标签，航空公司也不知道它属于谁。

lines.t: Transferring baggage from check-in to departure gates to arrival gates to baggage claim is a delicate piece of timing.
lines.zh: 将行李从登机口转移到登机口、到达口再到行李领取处是一个微妙的时机。
cloze: Transferring baggage from check-in to
gates to arrival gates to baggage claim is a delicate piece of timing.

lines.t: If the system moves too slowly, the bags won't make connecting flights.
lines.zh: 如果系统移动太慢，行李将无法转机。

lines.t: If it's too fast, the bags may make the connection, but the passengers might miss the flight.
lines.zh: 如果速度太快，行李可能会转机，但乘客可能会错过航班。
cloze: If it's too fast, the bags may make the
, but the passengers might miss the flight.

lines.t: Each airport has its own way of allotting how much time a bag needs to move in transit.
lines.zh: 每个机场都有自己的方式来分配行李在运输过程中需要多长时间。

lines.t: Some airports have sophisticated automated systems, including scanners that read baggage labels, destination coded vehicles that load and unload the bags without stopping, and sorting machines that route baggage to the appropriate gate.
lines.zh: 一些机场拥有先进的自动化系统，包括读取行李标签的扫描仪、不间断装卸行李的目的地编码车辆，以及将行李运送到适当登机口的分拣机。
cloze: Some airports have

automated systems, including scanners that read baggage labels, destination coded vehicles that load and unload the bags without stopping, and sorting machines that route baggage to the appropriate gate.

lines.t: Even so, all that technology may not save your baggage tag from being torn off on the conveyor belt, making you the owner of a bag with no name.
lines.zh: 即便如此，所有这些技术都可能无法避免您的行李标签在传送带上被撕下，从而使您成为一个没有名字的行李的主人。

lines.t: Once a bag goes missing and the passenger files a claim, the bag is declared mishandled by the carrier.
lines.zh: 一旦行李丢失并且乘客提出索赔，承运人就会宣布该行李处理不当。
cloze: Once a bag goes missing and the passenger files a claim, the bag is declared
by the carrier.

lines.t: Mishandled refers to bags that have been delayed, lost, stolen or damaged.
lines.zh: 处理不当是指行李被延误、丢失、被盗或损坏。

lines.t: Most delayed bags are only one flight behind their owners and can be delivered within 24 hours.
lines.zh: 大多数延误的行李仅比其主人晚一趟航班，并且可以在 24 小时内送达。
cloze: Most delayed bags are only one flight behind their owners and can be
within 24 hours.

lines.t: The other bags are examined by airline employees for clues to their ownership and destination.
lines.zh: 航空公司员工检查其他行李，寻找其所有权和目的地的线索。

lines.t: If the mystery is solved, those bags are returned to their owners within four or five days.
lines.zh: 如果谜团解开，这些袋子将在四五天内归还给它们的主人。
cloze: If the mystery is solved, those bags are
to their owners within four or five days.

lines.t: Bags with no destination code or identification tag are shipped to a central warehouse and undergo a comprehensive baggage tracing process over the next 90 days.
lines.zh: 没有目的地代码或识别标签的行李将被运送到中央仓库，并在接下来的 90 天内接受全面的行李追踪流程。

lines.t: Airlines inventory their mishandled baggage, and many use a database to match the contents with owners' descriptions.
lines.zh: 航空公司会对处理不当的行李进行清点，许多航空公司使用数据库将内容与所有者的描述进行匹配。
cloze: Airlines inventory their mishandled baggage, and many use a database to match the contents with owners'

lines.t: It takes about three months to go from missing inaction to irretrievably lost.
lines.zh: 从思念无所作为到无可挽回的迷失大约需要三个月的时间。

lines.t: Once that happens, the bags are donated to charity, sold at auction, or purchased by a company which sells them to the public.

lines.t: You've probably been with someone who ignored you while interacting with his or her smartphone, and you've probably engaged in this behavior yourself.
lines.zh: 您可能遇到过在与他或她的智能手机互动时忽略您的人，并且您自己也可能有这种行为。
cloze: You've probably been with someone who ignored you while
with his or her smartphone, and you've probably engaged in this behavior yourself.

lines.t: In a recent survey, nine out of ten respondents said they'd used their smartphone during their most recent social activity.
lines.zh: 在最近的一项调查中，十分之九的受访者表示他们在最近的社交活动中使用了智能手机。

lines.t: There's also evidence that this behavior is socially harmful.
lines.zh: 还有证据表明这种行为对社会有害。
cloze: There's also evidence that this
is socially harmful.

lines.t: It can leave people less satisfied with their face-to-face interactions, and it can generate feelings of resentment and jealousy.
lines.zh: 它可能会让人们对面对面的互动不太满意，并可能产生怨恨和嫉妒的感觉。

lines.t: Now, the Journal of Applied Social Psychology has published a new study exploring the reasons for these effects.
lines.zh: 现在，《应用社会心理学杂志》发表了一项新研究，探讨了这些影响的原因。
cloze: Now, the Journal of Applied Social Psychology has published a new study
the reasons for these effects.

lines.t: The study included 128 mostly female student participants.
lines.zh: 该研究包括 128 名参与者，其中大部分是女性。

lines.t: The participants watched a three-minute animation in which two cartoon figures interacted and engaged in a conversation.
lines.zh: 参与者观看了一段三分钟的动画，其中两个卡通人物互动并进行对话。
cloze: The participants watched a three-minute animation in which two cartoon figures interacted and engaged in a

lines.t: The conversation couldn't be heard, but could be detected through mouth movements.
lines.zh: 谈话内容听不到，但可以通过嘴巴的动作察觉到。

lines.t: Participants had to imagine themselves as the closest figure in the video, and then make judgments about the conversations and how they felt about their conversation partners.
lines.zh: 参与者必须将自己想象成视频中最接近的人物，然后对对话以及他们对对话伙伴的感受做出判断。
cloze: Participants had to imagine themselves as the closest figure in the video, and then make judgments about the
and how they felt about their conversation partners.

lines.t: In one version of the experiment, the phone of the participant's conversation partner remained unused on the table throughout the conversation.
lines.zh: 在实验的一个版本中，参与者的对话伙伴的电话在整个对话过程中一直放在桌子上未使用。

lines.t: In another version, their partner's attention was quickly drawn to something on their phone, and they spent the rest of the time interacting with their phone.
lines.zh: 在另一个版本中，他们的伴侣的注意力很快就被手机上的某些东西吸引，他们把剩下的时间都花在了与手机互动上。
cloze: In another version, their partner's attention was quickly drawn to something on their phone, and they spent the rest of the time
with their phone.

lines.t: A third version involved the participant's partner alternating between periods of interaction with their phone and periods where they ignored their phone.
lines.zh: 第三个版本涉及参与者的伴侣在与手机互动的时期和忽略手机的时期之间交替。

lines.t: If you've experienced the similar situation, you probably won't be surprised by the results of the experiments.
lines.zh: 如果您经历过类似的情况，您可能不会对实验结果感到惊讶。
cloze: If you've experienced the similar situation, you probably won't be surprised by the results of the

lines.t: The participants had a negative view of phone use during social interactions.
lines.zh: 参与者对社交互动中使用手机持负面看法。

lines.t: The more it was present, the worse they considered both the quality of the interaction and the quality of the relationship.
lines.zh: 它出现的越多，他们认为互动的质量和关系的质量就越差。
cloze: The more it was present, the worse they considered both the quality of the interaction and the quality of the

lines.t: The researchers believed that focusing on one's phone instead of the person one is with has this effect because it's seen as a form of social exclusion.
lines.zh: 研究人员认为，专注于手机而不是身边的人会产生这种效果，因为这被视为一种社会排斥形式。

lines.t: They assert that the behavior is analogous to when people have no choice but to eat alone in the school cafeteria.
lines.zh: 他们声称这种行为类似于人们别无选择只能在学校食堂独自吃饭。
cloze: They assert that the behavior is analogous to when people have no choice but to eat alone in the school

lines.t: The twist is that this exclusion occurs while sharing a physical encounter and having a conversation.
lines.zh: 奇怪的是，这种排斥发生在分享身体接触和交谈时。

lines.t: Researchers found that the behavior had adverse effects on participants' sense of belonging, need for meaning and self-esteem.
lines.zh: 研究人员发现，这种行为会对参与者的归属感、意义需求和自尊产生不利影响。
cloze: Researchers found that the behavior had adverse effects on participants' sense of belonging, need for meaning and

lines.t: These negative effects are similar to those caused by traditional forms of social exclusion.
lines.zh: 这些负面影响与传统形式的社会排斥造成的负面影响类似。

lines.t: The new findings are important because they elaborate our understanding of a subtle but common aspect of our daily experience.
lines.zh: 新发现很重要，因为它们阐述了我们对日常经历中微妙但常见的方面的理解。
cloze: The new findings are important because they elaborate our
of a subtle but common aspect of our daily experience.

lines.t: This common behavior can create vicious cycles of detachment even as we try to connect with others.
lines.zh: 即使我们试图与他人建立联系，这种常见的行为也会造成疏离的恶性循环。

lines.t: More and more people travel for a variety of reasons.
lines.zh: 越来越多的人出于各种原因出行。
cloze: More and more people travel for a
of reasons.

lines.t: Many are tourists, but many venture for some personal or professional business.
lines.zh: 许多人是游客，但许多人冒险从事一些个人或专业业务。

lines.t: Whatever the reason for traveling, a common complaint of travelers is the impersonal accommodations they find.
lines.zh: 无论旅行的原因是什么，旅行者普遍抱怨的就是他们发现的住宿条件不人性化。
cloze: Whatever the reason for traveling, a common complaint of travelers is the impersonal
they find.

lines.t: After spending five consecutive nights in five similar hotels, the business traveler may find it difficult to remember what happened from day to day or even what towns were visited.
lines.zh: 在五家类似的酒店连续住了五晚后，商务旅行者可能会发现很难记住每天发生的事情，甚至很难记住访问过哪些城镇。

lines.t: And the tourists may get the mistaken impression that all cities are pretty much the same, at least as far as decoration, food and service are concerned.
lines.zh: 游客可能会误以为所有城市都差不多，至少在装饰、食物和服务方面是如此。
cloze: And the tourists may get the mistaken impression that all cities are pretty much the same, at least as far as
, food and service are concerned.

lines.t: To combat this sense of impersonal sameness, travelers are taking advantage of in-home hospitality or bed-and-breakfast arrangements.
lines.zh: 为了消除这种非个人化的千篇一律的感觉，旅行者正在利用家庭招待或住宿加早餐的安排。

lines.t: B&Bs, I mean, bed-and-breakfast arrangements, are private homes which offer lodging and breakfast in a very personalized friendly setting.
lines.zh: B&B，我的意思是，住宿加早餐安排，是私人住宅，在非常个性化的友好环境中提供住宿和早餐。
cloze: B&Bs, I mean,
arrangements, are private homes which offer lodging and breakfast in a very personalized friendly setting.

lines.t: For decades, B&Bs have been the classic way to visit Europe, especially the British Isles.
lines.zh: 几十年来，住宿加早餐旅馆一直是游览欧洲（尤其是不列颠群岛）的经典方式。

lines.t: And in fact, they are not really a new idea in America.
lines.zh: 事实上，它们在美国并不是什么新想法。

lines.t: The tradition dates back to colonial times when inns were few and far between, and the weary traveler had to depend on the kindness of strangers for a meal and a bed.
lines.zh: 这一传统可以追溯到殖民时期，当时旅馆很少，而且距离很远，疲惫的旅行者不得不依靠陌生人的好意来获得食物和床铺。

lines.t: But the revival of B&Bs as desirable accommodations is a fairly recent phenomenon.
lines.zh: 但民宿重新成为理想的住宿场所是最近才出现的现象。
cloze: But the revival of B&Bs as desirable
is a fairly recent phenomenon.

lines.t: If the idea of operating a B&B arouses your interest, there are several factors to consider before plunging into this business.
lines.zh: 如果经营民宿的想法引起了您的兴趣，那么在投入这项业务之前需要考虑几个因素。

lines.t: The first consideration is your property, not only the building itself, but the location.
lines.zh: 首先要考虑的是您的财产，不仅是建筑物本身，还有位置。
cloze: The first
is your property, not only the building itself, but the location.

lines.t: If you live near a famous historical site or in a popular destination such as New York City or Washington D.C., your home can be fairly simple yet still do well as a B&B.
lines.zh: 如果您住在著名的历史遗址附近或纽约市或华盛顿特区等热门目的地，您的家可以相当简单，但作为住宿加早餐酒店仍然很不错。

lines.t: On the other hand, if your home is architecturally unique or has facilities for the traveler such as a private entrance, private bath or swimming pool, people may be willing to go some distance to reach you.
lines.zh: 另一方面，如果您的家具有独特的建筑风格或为旅行者提供设施，例如私人入口、私人浴室或游泳池，那么人们可能愿意走一段距离才能到达您。
cloze: On the other hand, if your home is
unique or has facilities for the traveler such as a private entrance, private bath or swimming pool, people may be willing to go some distance to reach you.

lines.t: Another important factor is the lifestyle of you and your family.
lines.zh: 另一个重要因素是您和您家人的生活方式。

lines.t: You must take into account whether all members of the family truly enjoy visitors, want to repeatedly discuss local sites and activities, and have the time and energy to handle the additional cooking, cleaning, laundry and the book keeping involved.
lines.zh: 您必须考虑所有家庭成员是否真正喜欢游客，想要反复讨论当地景点和活动，并有时间和精力处理额外的烹饪、清洁、洗衣和簿记工作。
cloze: You must take into account whether all members of the family truly enjoy visitors, want to repeatedly discuss local sites and activities, and have the time and energy to handle the
cooking, cleaning, laundry and the book keeping involved.

lines.t: The final consideration is a financial one.
lines.zh: 最后的考虑是财务方面的。

lines.t: Potential B&B hosts must be realistic about opportunities for income.
lines.zh: 潜在的民宿主人必须对收入机会持现实态度。
cloze: Potential B&B hosts must be realistic about
for income.

lines.t: While B&Bs usually have low initial costs, experts estimate it would take at least five rooms rented regularly for the host to earn a living from B&B.
lines.zh: 虽然民宿的初始成本通常较低，但专家估计，主人至少需要定期租用五个房间才能靠民宿谋生。

lines.t: Hi, Tony.
lines.zh: 嗨，托尼。

lines.t: Today we're talking about how managers can get along better with young people at work.
lines.zh: 今天我们谈论的是管理者如何在工作中与年轻人更好地相处。

lines.t: We often hear young people today have a poor work ethic.
lines.zh: 我们经常听到当今年轻人的职业道德很差。
cloze: We often hear young
have a poor work ethic.

lines.t: That's not really justified though, is it?
lines.zh: 但这其实并不合理，不是吗？

lines.t: Not really.
lines.zh: 并不真地。

lines.t: In reality, young people of this age group are as varied and multifaceted as any other generation.
lines.zh: 事实上，这个年龄段的年轻人与其他一代人一样具有多样性和多面性。

lines.t: Yeah, but if you are struggling to work with young people in your workspace, what can you do?
lines.zh: 是的，但是如果你在工作场所与年轻人一起工作时遇到困难，你能做什么？
cloze: Yeah, but if you are struggling to work with
in your workspace, what can you do?

lines.t: Well, it's essential to connect with them, to learn about their values.
lines.zh: 嗯，有必要与他们联系，了解他们的价值观。

lines.t: It's also really important to recognize the way young people want to balance their work life with their personal life.
lines.zh: 认识到年轻人想要平衡工作生活与个人生活的方式也非常重要。
cloze: It's also
to recognize the way young people want to balance their work life with their personal life.

lines.t: So, they generally don't want to defer happiness in return for career advancement?
lines.zh: 那么，他们通常不想推迟幸福来换取职业发展？

lines.t: Absolutely.
lines.zh: 绝对地。

lines.t: They are not willing to sacrifice their personal lives for their work lives.
lines.zh: 他们不愿意为了工作生活而牺牲个人生活。

lines.t: And this leads people to equate that with an unwillingness to work hard.
lines.zh: 这导致人们将其等同于不愿意努力工作。
cloze: And this leads people to equate that with an
to work hard.

lines.t: Right, but that couldn't be further from the truth, could it?
lines.zh: 是的，但这与事实相差甚远，不是吗？

lines.t: Young people will work extremely hard during their defined work hours.
lines.zh: 年轻人会在规定的工作时间内极其努力地工作。
cloze: Young people will work
during their defined work hours.

lines.t: But they expect to have their time off, like weekends and nights, free from work.
lines.zh: 但他们希望有休息时间，比如周末和晚上，不用工作。

lines.t: So, how should managers go about assessing young people's productivity?
lines.zh: 那么，管理者应该如何评估年轻人的生产力呢？
cloze: So, how should managers go about assessing young

lines.t: Generally, young people believe their productivity should not be measured by the number of hours they work—since someone can work for 8 hours and accomplish next to nothing of significance for the company.
lines.zh: 一般来说，年轻人认为他们的生产力不应该用工作时间来衡量——因为有人可以工作 8 小时，但对公司几乎没有任何意义。

lines.t: Instead, young people measure their productivity levels by the quality of the work they perform.
lines.zh: 相反，年轻人通过工作的质量来衡量他们的生产力水平。
cloze: Instead, young people measure their
by the quality of the work they perform.

lines.t: But we often hear that young people want to feel more than just being a part of a big machine.
lines.zh: 但我们经常听说年轻人想要的不仅仅是成为一台大机器的一部分。

lines.t: Such a perspective can be hard to discredit, can't it?
lines.zh: 这样的观点很难被质疑，不是吗？
cloze: Such a perspective can be hard to
it?

lines.t: It's important to legitimize their work.
lines.zh: 使他们的工作合法化很重要。

lines.t: Young workers want to work on projects that matter to themselves, the company or the world at large.
lines.zh: 年轻员工希望从事对自己、公司或整个世界都重要的项目。
cloze: want to work on projects that matter to themselves, the company or the world at large.

lines.t: They must feel the need to stay working at a company whose values align with their own.
lines.zh: 他们必须感到有必要留在一家价值观与自己一致的公司工作。

lines.t: Thanks for your advice.
lines.zh: 谢谢你的建议。

B) They don't get along with managers

lines.t: Many restaurants are trying to persuade customers to eat more sustainably, moving away from environmentally unfriendly meat towards greener dishes.
lines.zh: 许多餐馆正试图说服顾客以更可持续的方式饮食，从不环保的肉类转向更环保的菜肴。
cloze: Many restaurants are trying to persuade customers to eat more sustainably, moving away from
unfriendly meat towards greener dishes.

lines.t: Although it sounds counterintuitive, restaurants which include specific vegetarian sections on their menus may be unintentionally encouraging customers to eat meat, a new study suggests.
lines.zh: 一项新的研究表明，尽管这听起来有悖常理，但在菜单上包含特定素食部分的餐厅可能无意中鼓励顾客吃肉。

lines.t: Behavioral scientist Linda Bacon, one of the study's authors, said restaurants can have a positive impact on the environment by encouraging their customers to choose more plant-based food and less meat.
lines.zh: 该研究的作者之一、行为科学家琳达·培根表示，餐馆可以通过鼓励顾客选择更多的植物性食品和更少的肉类来对环境产生积极影响。
cloze: Behavioral scientist Linda Bacon, one of the study's authors, said restaurants can have a positive impact on the
by encouraging their customers to choose more plant-based food and less meat.

lines.t: However, our findings suggest that while certain restaurant menu designs can encourage some consumers to make pro-environmental food choices, they can have the opposite effect on others.
lines.zh: 然而，我们的研究结果表明，虽然某些餐厅的菜单设计可以鼓励一些消费者选择环保食品，但它们可能会对其他消费者产生相反的影响。

lines.t: The study involved 750 people, half of whom frequently ate vegetarian food, and half of whom rarely ate it.
lines.zh: 这项研究涉及 750 人，其中一半人经常吃素食，一半人很少吃素食。
cloze: The study involved 750 people, half of whom frequently ate
food, and half of whom rarely ate it.

lines.t: No vegetarians were included.
lines.zh: 不包括素食者。

lines.t: They were given different menus and asked to choose a meal as if they were eating out with friends.
lines.zh: 他们得到了不同的菜单，并被要求选择一顿饭，就像和朋友一起出去吃饭一样。
cloze: They were given
menus and asked to choose a meal as if they were eating out with friends.

lines.t: Placing vegetarian dishes in a separate section did not have a significant effect on the choices made by infrequent vegetarian food eaters.
lines.zh: 将素食菜肴放在单独的区域对于不常吃素食的人的选择没有显着影响。

lines.t: But it did have a notable effect on the frequent eaters, lowering their chance of picking a vegetarian option by 65%.
lines.zh: 但它确实对经常进食的人产生了显着影响，使他们选择素食的机会降低了 65%。
cloze: But it did have a notable effect on the frequent eaters, lowering their chance of picking a
option by 65%.

lines.t: The researchers also discovered that presenting a vegetarian dish as the chef's recommendation or including a more appealing description of a non-meat meal leads to a greater proportion of infrequent vegetarian eaters choosing a vegetarian option.
lines.zh: 研究人员还发现，将素食菜肴作为厨师的推荐或对非肉餐进行更吸引人的描述会导致更多不常吃素的人选择素食。

lines.t: But again, these altered menu designs backfired with those who ate vegetarian food more frequently, leading them to be less likely to choose a vegetarian dish.
lines.zh: 但同样，这些改变的菜单设计对那些经常吃素食的人来说适得其反，导致他们不太可能选择素食菜肴。
cloze: But again, these altered menu designs backfired with those who ate vegetarian food more frequently, leading them to be less likely to choose a
dish.

lines.t: Nottingham Trent University and the Chinese Academy of Sciences have been trying to find a way to prevent deadly outdoor air pollution from penetrating indoors.
lines.zh: 诺丁汉特伦特大学和中国科学院一直在努力寻找一种方法来防止致命的室外空气污染渗透到室内。
cloze: Nottingham Trent University and the Chinese Academy of Sciences have been trying to find a way to prevent deadly outdoor air pollution from
indoors.

lines.t: They found that if pollution is frozen to around minus 18 degrees Celsius in a condensing tube, the particles gather together and fall to the bottom, allowing fresh, clean air to pass through.
lines.zh: 他们发现，如果污染物在冷凝管中冻结至-18摄氏度左右，颗粒就会聚集在一起并落到底部，让新鲜、清洁的空气通过。

lines.t: Their method was able to remove 99% of pollutants.
lines.zh: 他们的方法能够去除 99% 的污染物。
cloze: Their method was able to remove 99% of

lines.t: It is hoped that the work could pave the way for simple modification of air conditioning units, so that they can also clean polluted indoor air.
lines.zh: 希望这项工作能为空调机组的简单改造铺平道路，让它们也能净化被污染的室内空气。

lines.t: Outdoor air pollution in cities is a global problem, whether it be haze plaguing Kolkata or poor air impacting the health of children in London schools.
lines.zh: 城市的室外空气污染是一个全球性问题，无论是困扰加尔各答的雾霾，还是影响伦敦学校儿童健康的不良空气。
cloze: Outdoor air pollution in cities is a global problem, whether it be haze plaguing Kolkata or poor air
the health of children in London schools.

lines.t: While there are some existing technologies to purify indoor air, they can be inefficient, expensive, or produce harmful byproducts.
lines.zh: 虽然现有一些技术可以净化室内空气，但它们可能效率低下、成本高昂，或者会产生有害的副产品。

lines.t: When outdoor air quality is poor, people tend to spend even more time indoors, but outdoor pollution also leads to indoor pollution, and people still suffer.
lines.zh: 当室外空气质量较差时，人们往往会在室内度过更多的时间，但室外污染也会导致室内污染，人们仍然深受其害。
cloze: When outdoor air quality is poor, people tend to spend even more time indoors, but outdoor
also leads to indoor pollution, and people still suffer.

lines.t: It is estimated that pollution is linked to over 40,000 early deaths in Britain each year.
lines.zh: 据估计，英国每年有超过 40,000 人过早死亡与污染有关。

lines.t: Professor Gang Pan of the Chinese Academy of Sciences said, “We have shown in our experiments that simply by circulating polluted air through a small freezing chamber, we can remove most of the fine particles and gas pollutants.
lines.zh: 中国科学院潘刚教授表示：“我们的实验表明，只需将受污染的空气循环通过一个小型冷冻室，就可以去除大部分细颗粒和气体污染物。
cloze: Professor Gang Pan of the Chinese Academy of Sciences said, “We have shown in our experiments that simply by
polluted air through a small freezing chamber, we can remove most of the fine particles and gas pollutants.

lines.t: Our study makes it possible to add an air cleaner option to household appliances in areas which might experience extremely poor air conditions.
lines.zh: 我们的研究使得在空气条件极差的地区为家用电器添加空气净化器选项成为可能。

lines.t: By controlling indoor air pollution and improving air quality in this way, this work could be greatly beneficial to public health.”
lines.zh: 通过这种方式控制室内空气污染并改善空气质量，这项工作将对公众健康大有裨益。”
cloze: By controlling indoor air pollution and improving air quality in this way, this work could be greatly
to public health.”

lines.t: Research recently carried out by my team suggests that fish may be self-aware.
lines.zh: 我的团队最近进行的研究表明鱼可能具有自我意识。
cloze: Research recently carried out by my team suggests that fish may be

lines.t: A certain species of fish recently passed the well-known mirror test—this is a test that demonstrates self-recognition in the animals.
lines.zh: 某种鱼类最近通过了著名的镜子测试——这是一项展示动物自我识别能力的测试。

lines.t: Only a few animals, such as humans, apes, dolphins and some birds can recognise themselves in a mirror, and only these animals capable of self-recognition will attempt to remove marks placed on their skin after noticing them in their reflection.
lines.zh: 只有少数动物，例如人类、猿、海豚和一些鸟类可以在镜子中认出自己，并且只有这些具有自我识别能力的动物在注意到镜子中的自己后，才会尝试去除皮肤上的标记。
cloze: Only a few animals, such as humans, apes, dolphins and some birds can recognise themselves in a mirror, and only these animals capable of
will attempt to remove marks placed on their skin after noticing them in their reflection.

lines.t: This ability suggests the level of higher intelligence and awareness.
lines.zh: 这种能力表明更高的智力和意识水平。

lines.t: This is not shown by children until around 18 months.
lines.zh: 儿童直到 18 个月左右才会表现出这一点。
cloze: This is not shown by
until around 18 months.

lines.t: Until now, no fish has demonstrated the ability, but our experiments show the fish in question will scrape up against hard surfaces to remove marks placed on its body by our researchers after viewing itself in a mirror.
lines.zh: 到目前为止，还没有鱼表现出这种能力，但我们的实验表明，这种鱼在镜子中观察自己后，会刮擦坚硬的表面，以去除我们的研究人员在其身体上留下的痕迹。

lines.t: The behaviours we observe leave little doubt that this fish behaviourally fulfils all criteria of the mirror test as originally laid out.
lines.zh: 我们观察到的行为毫无疑问表明这条鱼的行为符合最初制定的镜子测试的所有标准。
cloze: The
we observe leave little doubt that this fish behaviourally fulfils all criteria of the mirror test as originally laid out.

lines.t: The fish in our study never attempted to remove the marks when no mirror was present or when the marks were just placed on the mirror.
lines.zh: 当没有镜子存在或标记刚刚放在镜子上时，我们研究中的鱼从未尝试去除标记。

lines.t: Unmarked fish also did not attempt to remove marks from themselves when interacting with a marked fish on the other side of a window.
lines.zh: 当与窗户另一侧有标记的鱼互动时，未标记的鱼也不会尝试去除自己的标记。
cloze: Unmarked fish also did not attempt to remove marks from themselves when
with a marked fish on the other side of a window.

lines.t: These results show either that fish are self-aware or that the mirror test, which is considered to be the gold standard test used to denote higher intelligence, may be flawed.
lines.zh: 这些结果表明，要么鱼具有自我意识，要么镜子测试（被认为是用来表示较高智力的黄金标准测试）可能存在缺陷。

lines.t: What is less clear is whether these behaviours should be considered as evidence that fish are self-aware, even though in the past, these same behaviours have been interpreted as self-awareness in so many other animals.
lines.zh: 不太清楚的是，这些行为是否应该被视为鱼类具有自我意识的证据，尽管在过去，这些相同的行为在许多其他动物中被解释为自我意识。
cloze: What is less clear is whether these behaviours should be considered as evidence that fish are self-aware, even though in the past, these same behaviours have been interpreted as
in so many other animals.

lines.t: Depending on your position, you might reject the interpretation that these behaviours in a fish satisfy passing the test at all.
lines.zh: 根据您的立场，您可能会拒绝认为鱼的这些行为根本满足通过测试的解释。

lines.t: But on what objective basis can you do this when the behaviours they show are so functionally similar to those of other species that have passed the test?
lines.zh: 但是，当它们表现出的行为在功能上与通过测试的其他物种如此相似时，你能在什么客观基础上做到这一点呢？
cloze: But on what objective basis can you do this when the behaviours they show are so
similar to those of other species that have passed the test?

lines.t: Results from our research raise more questions than answers.
lines.zh: 我们的研究结果提出的问题多于答案。

lines.t: What if self-awareness develops like an onion, building layer upon layer rather than appearing all at once?
lines.zh: 如果自我意识像洋葱一样发展，一层又一层地发展而不是一下子全部出现呢？
cloze: What if
develops like an onion, building layer upon layer rather than appearing all at once?

lines.t: Perhaps, in order to explore self-awareness further, we should stop looking at responses to the mirror as a decisive test.
lines.zh: 也许，为了进一步探索自我意识，我们应该停止将对镜子的反应视为决定性的测试。

lines.t: Only with a richer theory of the self and a larger test battery will we be able to determine all of the various levels of self-awareness, including where exactly fish fit in.
lines.zh: 只有拥有更丰富的自我理论和更大的测试电池，我们才能确定所有不同层次的自我意识，包括鱼到底适合什么。
cloze: Only with a richer theory of the self and a larger test battery will we be able to determine all of the various levels of
, including where exactly fish fit in.

B) It reflects distinct traits in animal behaviour
C) It demonstrates animals5 ability to recognise themselves

C) It removes marks from itself to show self-awareness

lines.t: Reading with a young child is important, but does it matter whether you read from an electronic book or traditional print?
lines.zh: 与幼儿一起阅读很重要，但阅读电子书还是传统印刷品重要吗？
cloze: Reading with a young child is important, but does it matter whether you read from an electronic book or
print?

lines.t: As any parent knows, small children are generally keen on screens, so the finding from a new study that very young children enjoy electronic books more than printed picture books may not come as a huge surprise.
lines.zh: 任何家长都知道，小孩子通常都热衷于屏幕，因此一项新研究发现，年幼的孩子比印刷图画书更喜欢电子书，这可能并不令人感到意外。

lines.t: But the following additional findings might: both parents and children behave differently when reading electronic versus printed picture books, and the children who read the electronic books learned more.
lines.zh: 但以下额外的发现可能是：父母和孩子在阅读电子书和印刷图画书时的行为不同，并且阅读电子书的孩子学到了更多。
cloze: But the following additional findings might: both parents and children behave differently when reading electronic versus printed picture books, and the children who read the
books learned more.

lines.t: Previous studies of young children have suggested that electronic books, which incorporate extra features such as dictionaries and images that depict story events, may have advantages over print.
lines.zh: 之前对幼儿的研究表明，电子书可能比印刷书更具优势，因为电子书包含额外的功能，例如描述故事事件的词典和图像。

lines.t: In fact, multiple studies have found that electronic books support story comprehension and vocabulary gains beyond what is provided by printed books.
lines.zh: 事实上，多项研究发现，电子书对故事理解和词汇量增长的支持超过了印刷书籍。
cloze: In fact, multiple studies have found that electronic books support story
and vocabulary gains beyond what is provided by printed books.

lines.t: But there's also work suggesting that children sometimes invest less mental effort in learning from electronic books, and the parents talk less about content when sharing such books.
lines.zh: 但也有研究表明，孩子们有时在电子书学习上投入的精力较少，而父母在分享此类书籍时也较少谈论内容。

lines.t: The study we're looking at today aims to give us a better understanding of how good electronic books are for young children.
lines.zh: 我们今天看到的研究旨在让我们更好地了解电子书对幼儿的好处。
cloze: The study we're looking at today aims to give us a better
of how good electronic books are for young children.

lines.t: For this study, researchers videoed children aged 17 to 26 months reading with one of their parents.
lines.zh: 在这项研究中，研究人员拍摄了 17 至 26 个月大的儿童与其中一位父母一起阅读的视频。

lines.t: Each parent and child pair was randomly assigned to read either two educational electronic books or two printed books with the same content.
lines.zh: 每对父母和孩子被随机分配阅读两本教育电子书或两本内容相同的印刷书籍。
cloze: Each parent and child pair was randomly assigned to read either two
electronic books or two printed books with the same content.

lines.t: While the parent read the words in the printed books aloud, the electronic books had audio of voice actors reading the text.
lines.zh: 当家长大声朗读印刷书籍中的文字时，电子书中有配音演员朗读文字的音频。

lines.t: The researchers found that parents who read the printed books pointed more frequently to pages than parents who read the electronic books, but the opposite was true for the children.
lines.zh: 研究人员发现，阅读纸质书的父母比阅读电子书的父母更频繁地指向页面，但孩子的情况恰恰相反。
cloze: The researchers found that parents who read the printed books pointed more frequently to pages than parents who read the
books, but the opposite was true for the children.

lines.t: Children who read the electronic books also commented more on the content and learned more new words than the children who read printed books.
lines.zh: 阅读电子书的孩子比阅读纸质书的孩子对内容的评论更多，学到的新单词也更多。

lines.t: This greater learning is ascribed to greater engagement with the electronic books.
lines.zh: 这种更大的学习归因于对电子书的更多参与。
cloze: This greater learning is ascribed to greater
with the electronic books.

lines.t: It's important to note that the electronic books in the study were simple.
lines.zh: 值得注意的是，研究中的电子书很简单。

lines.t: While they included background music, animation and sound effects, there were no other extra features.
lines.zh: 虽然它们包括背景音乐、动画和音效，但没有其他额外的功能。
cloze: While they included
music, animation and sound effects, there were no other extra features.

lines.t: It's also important to note that there's research on older children finding that electronic books don't always bolster learning.
lines.zh: 同样重要的是要注意，对年龄较大的孩子的研究发现，电子书并不总是能促进学习。

lines.t: Parents and educators need to be aware extra features in electronic books may increase children's participation with them.
lines.zh: 家长和教育工作者需要意识到电子书中的额外功能可能会增加孩子们的参与度。
cloze: Parents and educators need to be aware extra features in electronic books may increase children's
with them.

lines.t: However, if these features don't draw attention to the educational content, they may not serve as a supportive feature.
lines.zh: 然而，如果这些功能不能引起人们对教育内容的关注，它们可能就不能作为支持性功能。

lines.t: Let me be honest with you.
lines.zh: 让我对你说实话。
cloze: Let me be
with you.

lines.t: If you are living your life full of regret, you are wasting your time.
lines.zh: 如果你的生活充满遗憾，那么你就是在浪费时间。

lines.t: Why would you go through life regretting the very decisions that made you who you are today?
lines.zh: 为什么你会终其一生对那些造就了今天的你的决定感到后悔呢？
cloze: Why would you go through life
the very decisions that made you who you are today?

lines.t: There are plenty of unfavorable decisions we’ve made, but does that mean we should regret them?
lines.zh: 我们做出了很多不利的决定，但这是否意味着我们应该后悔？

lines.t: No. I’ve had many moments where I sit and think about all the things I wish I could have done differently.
lines.zh: 不。我有很多时候会坐下来思考所有我希望自己能做得不同的事情。
cloze: No. I’ve had many moments where I sit and think about all the things I wish I could have done

lines.t: However, just because things could be different, it doesn’t necessarily mean they would be better.
lines.zh: 然而，仅仅因为事情可能会有所不同，并不一定意味着它们会更好。

lines.t: You don't have to continually be thinking of all your past decisions and whether or not you made the right one.
lines.zh: 你不必不断地思考你过去的所有决定以及你是否做出了正确的决定。
cloze: You don't have to continually be thinking of all your past
and whether or not you made the right one.

lines.t: You can't go back and change anything.
lines.zh: 你无法回去改变任何事情。

lines.t: So what's the point in worrying about it?
lines.zh: 那么担心这个有什么意义呢？
cloze: So what's the point in
about it?

lines.t: Every single decision you've ever made, positive or negative, has made you the person you are today.
lines.zh: 你所做的每一个决定，无论是积极的还是消极的，都造就了今天的你。

lines.t: We want to go back and change parts of our past, but what would be the benefit of that?
lines.zh: 我们想回到过去并改变一些过去，但这样做有什么好处呢？
cloze: We want to go back and change parts of our past, but what would be the
of that?

lines.t: We would have lost the valuable knowledge from the lessons we learned.
lines.zh: 我们将会失去从我们所学到的教训中获得的宝贵知识。

lines.t: There are reasons you make the choices you do, and that tells us about who you are.
lines.zh: 您做出选择是有原因的，这告诉我们您是谁。

lines.t: So when it comes to any decision in life, be unapologetically yourself, because at the end of the day, it was you who made that decision.
lines.zh: 因此，当涉及到生活中的任何决定时，请毫无歉意地为自己做决定，因为到最后，是你做出了这个决定。

lines.t: With less time spent focused on regrets, you will finally have time to focus on the more essential things in life.
lines.zh: 随着花在后悔上的时间减少，您最终将有时间关注生活中更重要的事情。

things in life.

lines.t: When a person tries to access a memory, their brains quickly examine everything stored in it to find the relevant information.
lines.zh: 当一个人试图访问记忆时，他们的大脑会快速检查存储在其中的所有内容以查找相关信息。
cloze: When a person tries to access a memory, their brains quickly examine everything stored in it to find the relevant

lines.t: But as we age, many of us have difficulty retrieving memories.
lines.zh: 但随着年龄的增长，我们中的许多人都很难恢复记忆。

lines.t: In a review published in the journal Trends in Cognitive Sciences on February 11, researchers propose an explanation for why this might be happening: the brains of older adults allocate more space to accumulated knowledge and have more material to navigate when attempting to access memories.
lines.zh: 在 2 月 11 日发表在《认知科学趋势》杂志上的一篇评论中，研究人员对为什么会发生这种情况提出了一种解释：老年人的大脑会分配更多的空间来积累知识，并且在尝试访问记忆时有更多的材料可供导航。
cloze: In a review published in the journal Trends in Cognitive Sciences on February 11, researchers propose an explanation for why this might be happening: the brains of older adults allocate more space to
knowledge and have more material to navigate when attempting to access memories.

lines.t: While this wealth of prior knowledge can make memory retrieval challenging, the researchers say it has its upsides — this life experience can aid with creativity and decision-making.
lines.zh: 虽然这些丰富的先验知识可能会给记忆检索带来挑战，但研究人员表示，它有其优点——这种生活经历可以帮助创造力和决策。

lines.t: Researchers Tarek Amer, Jordana Wynn and Lynn Hasher looked at several behavioral and brain imaging studies which show that older adults have difficulty suppressing information that is no longer relevant and that when searching for a specific memory, they often retrieve other irrelevant memories along with it.
lines.zh: 研究人员塔里克·阿梅尔（Tarek Amer）、乔丹娜·韦恩（Jordana Wynn）和林恩·哈舍尔（Lynn Hasher）研究了几项行为和大脑成像研究，这些研究表明，老年人很难抑制不再相关的信息，并且在寻找特定记忆时，他们经常会同时检索其他不相关的记忆。
cloze: Researchers Tarek Amer, Jordana Wynn and Lynn Hasher looked at several behavioral and brain imaging studies which show that older adults have difficulty suppressing
that is no longer relevant and that when searching for a specific memory, they often retrieve other irrelevant memories along with it.

lines.t: The studies also showed that when given a cognitive task, older adults rely more heavily on previous knowledge than younger adults do.
lines.zh: 研究还表明，当接受认知任务时，老年人比年轻人更依赖先前的知识。

lines.t: While the researchers focus primarily on the difficulties that these disorderly, crowded memories may pose, they also highlight a few situations in which these same memory patterns may be useful.
lines.zh: 虽然研究人员主要关注这些无序、拥挤的记忆可能带来的困难，但他们也强调了这些相同的记忆模式可能有用的几种情况。
cloze: While the researchers focus primarily on the
that these disorderly, crowded memories may pose, they also highlight a few situations in which these same memory patterns may be useful.

lines.t: "Evidence suggests that older adults show preserved, and at times enhanced, creativity as a function of enriched memories," the researchers write.
lines.zh: 研究人员写道：“有证据表明，随着记忆的丰富，老年人表现出保留的、有时甚至增强的创造力。”

lines.t: They further hypothesize that older adults may be well served by their prior knowledge when it comes to decision-making, where they can pull on their accumulated wisdom.
lines.zh: 他们进一步假设，老年人在决策时可能会受益于他们先前的知识，他们可以利用他们积累的智慧。
cloze: They further hypothesize that older adults may be well served by their prior knowledge when it comes to
, where they can pull on their accumulated wisdom.

lines.t: There are at least four major problems with work in America today.
lines.zh: 当今美国的工作至少存在四个主要问题。
cloze: There are at least four major problems with work in

lines.t: First, work can be alienating.
lines.zh: 首先，工作可能会让人疏远。

lines.t: Workers are often not in control of how they work, when they work, what is done with the goods and services they produce, and what is done with the profits made from their work.
lines.zh: 工人往往无法控制自己的工作方式、工作时间、生产的商品和服务的用途以及工作利润的用途。
cloze: Workers are often not in control of how they work, when they work, what is done with the goods and services they produce, and what is done with the
from their work.

lines.t: Second, workers are not paid the full value of their labor.
lines.zh: 其次，工人没有获得其劳动的全部价值。

lines.t: Real wages have not kept pace with productivity, driving economic inequality and a decline in labor's share of income.
lines.zh: 实际工资未能跟上生产率的步伐，导致经济不平等和劳动收入份额下降。
cloze: Real wages have not kept pace with
economic inequality and a decline in labor's share of income.

lines.t: Third, people are time poor.
lines.zh: 第三，人们时间匮乏。

lines.t: In the U.S., full-time employees work an average of 8.72 hours per day, despite productivity increases.
lines.zh: 在美国，尽管生产力有所提高，全职员工平均每天工作 8.72 小时。
cloze: In the U.S., full-time employees work an average of 8.72 hours per day, despite

lines.t: Long working hours contribute to the feeling of time poverty, which has an adverse effect on psychological well-being.
lines.zh: 长时间工作会让人产生时间匮乏的感觉，从而对心理健康产生不利影响。

lines.t: Fourth, automation puts jobs and wages at risk.
lines.zh: 第四，自动化使就业和工资面临风险。
cloze: puts jobs and wages at risk.

lines.t: Technological innovation could in theory liberate people from the 40-hour workweek.
lines.zh: 理论上，技术创新可以将人们从每周 40 小时的工作中解放出来。

lines.t: But unless changes are made to the structure of work, automation will simply exert downward pressure on wages and further diminish work opportunities.
lines.zh: 但除非工作结构发生改变，否则自动化只会给工资带来下行压力，并进一步减少工作机会。
cloze: But unless changes are made to the structure of work, automation will simply exert downward pressure on wages and further diminish

lines.t: So what can be done to alleviate these problems?
lines.zh: 那么可以采取什么措施来缓解这些问题呢？

lines.t: There are competing visions of the best way to arrive at a solution.
lines.zh: 对于达成解决方案的最佳方式存在着不同的看法。
cloze: There are
of the best way to arrive at a solution.

lines.t: One vision is what's known as the "post-work" position.
lines.zh: 一种愿景是所谓的“下班后”职位。

lines.t: The post-work theorists believe that work should not hold a central position in our lives or take up so much of our time.
lines.zh: 后工作理论家认为，工作不应该在我们的生活中占据中心地位，也不应该占据我们太多的时间。
cloze: The
believe that work should not hold a central position in our lives or take up so much of our time.

lines.t: They assert that although doing some work might be necessary, meaning, purpose and social value reside in the communities and relationships built and sustained outside of the workplace.
lines.zh: 他们声称，虽然做一些工作可能是必要的，但意义、目的和社会价值存在于工作场所之外建立和维持的社区和关系中。

lines.t: Thus, life should be seen as an end in itself.
lines.zh: 因此，生命本身应该被视为目的。
cloze: should be seen as an end in itself.

lines.t: Recent studies show that self-control and persistence increase academic outcomes independent of IQ.

of IQ.

lines.t: Even our personal beliefs about effort can affect academic outcomes.
lines.zh: 甚至我们个人对努力的信念也会影响学业成果。

lines.t: Children who think effort leads to achievement outperform those who believe ability is a fixed trait.
lines.zh: 那些认为努力会带来成就的孩子比那些相信能力是固定特征的孩子表现更好。
cloze: Children who think effort leads to
outperform those who believe ability is a fixed trait.

lines.t: Given the link between persistence and academic success, decisions about effort are particularly important in childhood.
lines.zh: 鉴于坚持与学业成功之间的联系，关于努力的决定在童年时期尤为重要。

lines.t: Yet relatively little research has explored how young children learn what's worth the effort.
lines.zh: 然而，相对较少的研究探讨了幼儿如何学习什么是值得付出努力的。
cloze: Yet relatively little research has explored how young
learn what's worth the effort.

lines.t: We all know that infants are keen observers of the social world.
lines.zh: 我们都知道，婴儿是社会世界的敏锐观察者。

lines.t: But they're not just idly watching; they are tiny learning machines.
lines.zh: 但他们并不只是袖手旁观，而是袖手旁观。它们是微型学习机器。

machines.

lines.t: They can generalize such abstract concepts as causal relationships and social roles from just a few examples.
lines.zh: 他们可以从几个例子中概括出因果关系和社会角色等抽象概念。

lines.t: Even a 15-month-old infant can outperform a high-level computer in such tasks.
lines.zh: 即使是 15 个月大的婴儿在此类任务中也能胜过高级计算机。

computer in such tasks.

lines.t: Could infants also make broad, generalizable inferences from a few examples when it comes to effort?
lines.zh: 当谈到努力时，婴儿是否也可以从几个例子中做出广泛的、普遍的推论？

lines.t: If so, then maybe persistence isn't simply a character trait.
lines.zh: 如果是这样，那么坚持也许不仅仅是一种性格特征。
cloze: If so, then maybe
isn't simply a character trait.

lines.t: Maybe it's flexible and adaptable based on social context.
lines.zh: 也许它是基于社会背景的灵活性和适应性。

lines.t: To explore this question, we showed 15-month-old babies one of two things: an experimenter working hard to achieve two different goals, or an experimenter who effortlessly reached each goal.
lines.zh: 为了探索这个问题，我们向 15 个月大的婴儿展示了以下两件事之一：一名实验者努力实现两个不同的目标，或者一名实验者毫不费力地实现了每个目标。
cloze: To explore this question, we showed 15-month-old babies one of two things: an experimenter working hard to achieve two different goals, or an
who effortlessly reached each goal.

lines.t: Then we introduced the baby to a novel "music" toy that seemed as if it could be activated by pushing a big button on top.
lines.zh: 然后我们向婴儿介绍了一种新颖的“音乐”玩具，似乎可以通过按下顶部的大按钮来激活它。

lines.t: The button could be pressed down but didn't actually activate anything.
lines.zh: 该按钮可以按下，但实际上并没有激活任何东西。

lines.t: Out of sight of the babies, we turned on the music toy with a hidden button so that they heard the toy making music.
lines.zh: 在婴儿看不见的地方，我们用一个隐藏的按钮打开音乐玩具，以便他们听到玩具发出的音乐。

lines.t: We gave the babies the music toy and left the room.
lines.zh: 我们给了孩子们音乐玩具，然后离开了房间。

lines.t: Then analysts, who didn't know which condition each baby was in, watched videotapes of the experiment and counted how many times babies tried to activate the toy by pressing the button.
lines.zh: 然后，不知道每个婴儿所处状况的分析人员观看了实验录像，并计算了婴儿尝试按下按钮来激活玩具的次数。

lines.t: Across one study and a preregistered duplication, babies who had seen an adult persist and succeed pushed the button about twice as many times as those who saw an adult effortlessly succeed.
lines.zh: 在一项研究和一项预先注册的重复研究中，看到成年人坚持不懈并取得成功的婴儿按下按钮的次数大约是看到成年人毫不费力地成功的婴儿的两倍。
cloze: Across one study and a
duplication, babies who had seen an adult persist and succeed pushed the button about twice as many times as those who saw an adult effortlessly succeed.

lines.t: In other words, babies learned that effort was valuable after watching just two examples of an adult working hard and succeeding.
lines.zh: 换句话说，婴儿在观看了两个成年人努力工作并取得成功的例子后就知道努力是有价值的。

lines.t: Part of what's exciting about this finding is that the babies didn't just imitate the adult's actions; instead, they generalized the value of effort to a novel task.
lines.zh: 这一发现令人兴奋的部分原因在于，婴儿不仅模仿成人的行为，而且还模仿成人的行为。相反，他们将努力的价值概括为新任务。

lines.t: Instead the babies learned from different examples of effortful actions that the new toy probably also required persistence.

lines.t: If chronic lateness has taken over your life and turned into a defining trait of who you are, it's likely that you're losing out on job offers, recreational opportunities, friendships and more.
lines.zh: 如果长期迟到已经占据了你的生活，并成为你的一个决定性特征，那么你很可能会失去工作机会、娱乐机会、友谊等等。
cloze: If chronic lateness has taken over your life and turned into a defining trait of who you are, it's likely that you're losing out on job offers,
opportunities, friendships and more.

lines.t: If you're showing up late to your own life, get organized, prioritize punctuality, and address any underlying causes.
lines.zh: 如果您在自己的生活中迟到，请组织起来，优先考虑守时，并解决任何根本原因。

lines.t: When you have to be somewhere, try to arrive 15 to 30 minutes before you need to.
lines.zh: 当您必须到达某个地方时，请尽量提前 15 到 30 分钟到达。
cloze: When you have to be
, try to arrive 15 to 30 minutes before you need to.

lines.t: If you always run late, that means you must be failing to account for something you always do.
lines.zh: 如果你总是迟到，那就意味着你一定没有考虑到你总是做的事情。

lines.t: Anticipate that by giving yourself extra time to arrive.
lines.zh: 通过给自己额外的时间到达来预计这一点。
cloze: Anticipate that by giving yourself extra time to

lines.t: Keep track of whether or not you actually do arrive early!
lines.zh: 记录一下您是否真的提前到达！

lines.t: You might find that leaving "early" gets you to places exactly on time.
lines.zh: 您可能会发现“早”出发可以让您准时到达目的地。
cloze: You might find that
"early" gets you to places exactly on time.

lines.t: Set two alarms.
lines.zh: 设置两个闹钟。

lines.t: Set one alarm that lets you know it's time to drop what you're doing, and a second alarm that means you need to walk out the door.
lines.zh: 设置一个闹钟，让你知道是时候放下手头的事情了，设置第二个闹钟，让你知道你需要走出家门。
cloze: Set one alarm that lets you know it's time to drop what you're doing, and a
alarm that means you need to walk out the door.

lines.t: Obey the alarms!
lines.zh: 遵守警报！

lines.t: As soon as the first alarm goes off, stop what you're doing.
lines.zh: 第一个闹钟一响，就停止你正在做的事情。

lines.t: If it's something you'll be coming back to, like a project for work, make a note to remind yourself where you left off.
lines.zh: 如果这是您将要返回的事情，例如工作项目，请记下以提醒自己上次离开的位置。

lines.t: Grab everything you need and make sure you know how to get where you're going.
lines.zh: 带上您需要的一切，并确保您知道如何到达目的地。
cloze: Grab
you need and make sure you know how to get where you're going.

lines.t: Aim to be out the door and on your way before the second alarm rings.
lines.zh: 争取在第二个警报响起之前走出门并上路。

lines.t: This will only work if you take the alarms seriously, so make sure you react as soon as you hear them.
lines.zh: 只有当您认真对待警报时，这才会起作用，因此请确保您在听到警报后立即做出反应。

lines.t: Prepare for the day ahead.
lines.zh: 为未来的一天做好准备。

lines.t: Have all of your notes and materials organized well in advance of each event so that all you have to do is grab them and go when it's the actual day.
lines.zh: 在每次活动之前将所有笔记和材料整理好，以便您所要做的就是在实际活动当天拿起它们并出发。
cloze: Have all of your notes and
organized well in advance of each event so that all you have to do is grab them and go when it's the actual day.

lines.t: If mornings are a struggle for you, do as much as you can to ready yourself the night before: before you go to bed, lay out your clothes and pack your bag for the next day.
lines.zh: 如果早上对你来说很困难，请在前一天晚上尽可能做好准备：睡觉前，把第二天要穿的衣服放好，收拾好行李。

lines.t: Learn to leave time in between tasks and meetings.
lines.zh: 学会在任务和会议之间留出时间。
cloze: Learn to leave time in between tasks and

lines.t: It soon becomes unbearable to shift between one meeting and another without a space in between.
lines.zh: 很快，在一场会议和另一场会议之间切换而中间没有间隔就变得令人难以忍受。

lines.t: If you overschedule yourself, however, you'll arrive late as soon as you hit a bump.
lines.zh: 然而，如果你给自己安排过多，一旦遇到困难你就会迟到。
cloze: If you
yourself, however, you'll arrive late as soon as you hit a bump.

lines.t: As well as giving you space, this time also acts as a buffer between events which can be "borrowed" from should you be held up in a prior meeting, allowing you to still get to the next one on time.
lines.zh: 除了为您提供空间外，这段时间还可以充当活动之间的缓冲区，如果您在之前的会议中被耽搁，可以“借用”这些时间，从而使您仍然可以准时参加下一个会议。

lines.t: Calculate transit time between activities and then add 10 to 30 minutes for unexpected delays.
lines.zh: 计算活动之间的交通时间，然后增加 10 到 30 分钟以防意外延误。
cloze: Calculate transit time between activities and then add 10 to 30 minutes for
delays.

lines.t: Do you think Bostonians put out the welcome mat?
lines.zh: 你认为波士顿人会铺出欢迎垫吗？
cloze: Do you think Bostonians put out the
mat?

lines.t: Do you find other cities to be more or less polite?
lines.zh: 您发现其他城市或多或少有礼貌吗？

lines.t: Different cities have different feels for visitors.
lines.zh: 不同的城市给游客带来不同的感受。
cloze: Different cities have
feels for visitors.

lines.t: Some are friendly and open.
lines.zh: 有些人很友好、开放。

lines.t: Some are formal and distant.
lines.zh: 有些是正式的、疏远的。

lines.t: Boston tends to seem hurried and sometimes a little rude.
lines.zh: 波士顿往往显得匆忙，有时甚至有点粗鲁。

lines.t: That's what some tourists have said.
lines.zh: 一些游客是这么说的。
cloze: That's what some
have said.

lines.t: One study found that people here are less willing to volunteer to help strangers than those residents of other U.S. cities.
lines.zh: 一项研究发现，与美国其他城市的居民相比，这里的人们不太愿意自愿帮助陌生人。

lines.t: Take a close look next time you're in Boston, and here are some of the things you'll probably see: people smoking in the subway stations despite the frequent reminders not to do so; pedestrians walking when the crosswalk lights say not to do so, ignoring the cars; car drivers speeding, making a loud noise with the horn, and occasionally cursing at each other; drivers who can't be bothered to find a place to park but instead simply turn on their blinker and stop in the middle of the street.
lines.zh: 下次您在波士顿时仔细观察，您可能会看到以下一些事情： 人们在地铁站吸烟，尽管经常提醒不要这样做；行人在人行横道灯亮时表示不要这样做，无视车辆；汽车司机超速行驶，大声鸣喇叭，偶尔还互相咒骂；司机懒得找地方停车，而只是打开方向灯，把车停在路中间。
cloze: Take a close look next time you're in Boston, and here are some of the things you'll probably see: people smoking in the subway stations despite the frequent reminders not to do so;

walking when the crosswalk lights say not to do so, ignoring the cars; car drivers speeding, making a loud noise with the horn, and occasionally cursing at each other; drivers who can't be bothered to find a place to park but instead simply turn on their blinker and stop in the middle of the street.

lines.t: Sometimes Bostonians seem like they're just too busy to be polite.
lines.zh: 有时波士顿人似乎太忙而没有礼貌。

lines.t: Why is the city like that?
lines.zh: 这座城市为何如此？

lines.t: Former U.S. Representative Chester Atkins says it's because the Puritan Founding Fathers were themselves impatient and bad-tempered and had little time for courtesy.
lines.zh: 前美国众议员切斯特·阿特金斯表示，这是因为清教徒开国元勋们本身缺乏耐心、脾气暴躁，几乎没有时间礼貌待人。

lines.t: That culture has carried down to the present day, he believes.
lines.zh: 他相信，这种文化一直延续到了今天。
cloze: That culture has carried down to the
day, he believes.

lines.t: Boston College professor Thomas O'Connor thinks a contributing factor is Boston's history as a city where each new group of immigrants was treated with suspicion and exclusion.
lines.zh: 波士顿学院教授托马斯·奥康纳认为，一个促成因素是波士顿这座城市的历史，每一个新移民群体都受到怀疑和排斥。

lines.t: That's given Boston a sense of clannishness and reserve, he thinks.
lines.zh: 他认为，这给波士顿带来了一种宗派和保守的感觉。
cloze: That's given Boston a sense of
and reserve, he thinks.

lines.t: The idea of a stranger greeting another stranger is simply not part of the local culture, he says.
lines.zh: 他说，一个陌生人问候另一个陌生人的想法根本不属于当地文化的一部分。

lines.t: People would begin a conversation with someone they know, but not with a stranger.
lines.zh: 人们会与他们认识的人开始对话，但不会与陌生人开始对话。
cloze: People would begin a
with someone they know, but not with a stranger.

lines.t: Ralph Whitehead, a professor of journalism at the University of Massachusetts at Amherst, thinks it's because Boston's upper class used manners to make class distinctions by being snobbish about manners.
lines.zh: 马萨诸塞大学阿默斯特分校的新闻学教授拉尔夫·怀特海德认为，这是因为波士顿的上层阶级通过对礼仪的势利来利用礼仪来区分阶级。

lines.t: Proper Bostonians made other people scornful of courtesy, he says.
lines.zh: 他说，正派的波士顿人让其他人蔑视礼貌。
cloze: Proper Bostonians made other people
of courtesy, he says.

lines.t: Some say that's just the way Boston is and that the city will never change.
lines.zh: 有人说波士顿就是这样，这座城市永远不会改变。

lines.t: Still, other cities with reputations for worse rudeness are trying hard to change their images.
lines.zh: 尽管如此，其他因粗鲁行为而闻名的城市正在努力改变自己的形象。
cloze: Still, other cities with
for worse rudeness are trying hard to change their images.

lines.t: Paris is one example where people are trying to be friendly.

lines.t: New York City is another; there, the city is trying to persuade subway riders to be more considerate.

lines.t: Logging into your email account can sometimes feel like trying to hack into the Pentagon.

lines.t: If you follow all of the guidelines, you need to use a different password for every one of your accounts; use an incomprehensible variety of letters, numbers, and symbols; sign up for two-step verification; and change every password every time one of them is compromised.
lines.zh: 如果您遵循所有准则，则需要为每个帐户使用不同的密码；使用各种难以理解的字母、数字和符号；注册两步验证；并在每次其中一个密码被泄露时更改每个密码。

lines.t: More often than not, you then have to choose photos that include a street sign, as this apparently provides solid evidence to your computer that you are, in fact, a human being.
lines.zh: 通常，您必须选择包含街道标志的照片，因为这显然为您的计算机提供了确凿的证据，表明您实际上是一个人。
cloze: More often than not, you then have to choose photos that include a street sign, as this apparently provides solid
to your computer that you are, in fact, a human being.

lines.t: It's no small wonder most of us forget our passwords more often than our keys.
lines.zh: 难怪我们大多数人忘记密码的次数比忘记钥匙的次数还要多。

lines.t: Now a new peer-reviewed study by researchers at Aalto University in Finland is attempting to figure out why we forget our passwords in order to help put an end to this frustrating phenomenon.
lines.zh: 现在，芬兰阿尔托大学的研究人员进行的一项新的同行评审研究正试图找出我们忘记密码的原因，以帮助结束这种令人沮丧的现象。
cloze: Now a new peer-reviewed study by researchers at Aalto University in Finland is attempting to figure out why we forget our passwords in order to help put an end to this
phenomenon.

lines.t: Their findings suggest that how likely you are to remember your password has less to do with the intricacy of the password itself and more to do with how often you anticipate using it.
lines.zh: 他们的研究结果表明，您记住密码的可能性与密码本身的复杂性关系不大，而与您预计使用密码的频率有关。

lines.t: Which is to say: you are far more likely to remember a complicated password if you know you'll frequently be using it to log into an account than you are to remember a simple password for an account that you don't expect to log into very often.
lines.zh: 也就是说：如果您知道自己会经常使用复杂的密码登录帐户，那么您更有可能记住复杂的密码，而不是记住您不希望经常登录的帐户的简单密码。
cloze: Which is to say: you are far more likely to remember a
password if you know you'll frequently be using it to log into an account than you are to remember a simple password for an account that you don't expect to log into very often.

lines.t: The researchers advise websites to include more of an incentive for users to log in more often in order to help them remember their secret codes.
lines.zh: 研究人员建议网站提供更多激励措施，鼓励用户更频繁地登录，以帮助他们记住密码。

lines.t: All societies are held together by seven universal moral rules, which include deferring to superiors and respecting the property of others, Oxford University has concluded.
lines.zh: 牛津大学得出结论，所有社会都由七项普遍的道德规则维系在一起，其中包括服从上级和尊重他人的财产。
cloze: All societies are held together by seven universal moral rules, which include deferring to superiors and
the property of others, Oxford University has concluded.

lines.t: Although many cultures are moving towards more liberal, less hierarchical organizations, the new research suggests that traditional power structures and basic values of charity and brotherhood are the cornerstones of successful societies.
lines.zh: 尽管许多文化正在走向更加自由、等级制度更少的组织，但新的研究表明，传统的权力结构以及慈善和兄弟情谊的基本价值观是成功社会的基石。

lines.t: The huge study of 60 different cultures around the world found that all communities operate under seven basic moral codes.
lines.zh: 对世界各地 60 种不同文化的大规模研究发现，所有社区都遵循七项基本道德准则。
cloze: The huge study of 60 different cultures around the world found that all
operate under seven basic moral codes.

lines.t: Those universal rules are: help your family, help your group, return favors, be brave, defer to superiors, divide resources fairly, and respect the property of others.
lines.zh: 这些普遍的规则是：帮助你的家人，帮助你的团体，回报他人，勇敢，服从上级，公平分配资源，尊重他人的财产。

lines.t: The character traits held for every kind of community, be they traditional hunter gatherers or advanced civilizations, helping to uphold civilized society and foster social cooperation, researchers found.
lines.zh: 研究人员发现，各种社区的性格特征，无论是传统的狩猎采集者还是先进的文明，都有助于维护文明社会并促进社会合作。
cloze: The character traits held for every kind of community, be they traditional hunter gatherers or advanced
, helping to uphold civilized society and foster social cooperation, researchers found.

lines.t: "Everyone everywhere shares a common moral code," said Dr. Oliver Scott Curry, lead author and senior researcher at Oxford.
lines.zh: “世界各地的每个人都有共同的道德准则，”牛津大学高级研究员奥利弗·斯科特·库里博士说。

lines.t: "These seven moral rules appear to be universal across cultures, because people face the same social problems.
lines.zh: “这七项道德规则似乎在不同文化中都是通用的，因为人们面临着相同的社会问题。
cloze: "These seven moral rules appear to be
across cultures, because people face the same social problems.

lines.t: Even if some of these traits look right-wing or conservative, for example, deferring to authority, left-wing people will still have a group loyalty and deference to someone or something.
lines.zh: 即使其中一些特征看起来是右翼或保守的，例如，服从权威，左翼人士仍然会具有群体忠诚度并尊重某人或某事。

lines.t: This shows there really is more that unites us than divides us."
lines.zh: 这表明，团结我们的因素确实多于分裂我们的因素。”
cloze: This shows there really is more that unites us than
us."

lines.t: The study published in Current Anthropology is the largest and most comprehensive and widespread survey of morals ever conducted and aimed to find out whether different societies had different versions of morality.
lines.zh: 发表在《当代人类学》上的这项研究是迄今为止规模最大、最全面、最广泛的道德调查，旨在找出不同社会是否有不同版本的道德。

lines.t: The team accessed the world's best archives to analyze accounts from more than 600 sources of 60 societies around the world.
lines.zh: 该团队访问了世界上最好的档案，分析了来自全球 60 个社团的 600 多个来源的账户。
cloze: The team accessed the world's best archives to analyze accounts from more than 600 sources of 60
around the world.

lines.t: They found that the seven rules were considered morally good in all societies and were observed across all continents, religions and politics.
lines.zh: 他们发现，这七项规则在所有社会中都被认为是道德良好的，并且在各大洲、宗教和政治领域都得到遵守。

lines.t: However, some communities valued certain rules more highly than others.
lines.zh: 然而，一些社区比其他社区更重视某些规则。
cloze: However, some
valued certain rules more highly than others.

lines.t: Dr. Curry hopes that this research helps to promote mutual understanding between people of different cultures and appreciation of what we have in common and how and why we differ.
lines.zh: 库里博士希望这项研究有助于促进不同文化背景的人们之间的相互理解，并了解我们的共同点以及差异的方式和原因。

lines.t: Co-author professor Harvey Whitehouse said social scientists should now set about testing the theory in the field, rather than relying on old data.
lines.zh: 合著者哈维·怀特豪斯教授表示，社会科学家现在应该着手在该领域测试该理论，而不是依赖旧数据。
cloze: Co-author
Harvey Whitehouse said social scientists should now set about testing the theory in the field, rather than relying on old data.

lines.t: "This study was based on historical descriptions of cultures around the world," he said.
lines.zh: “这项研究基于对世界各地文化的历史描述，”他说。

lines.t: "These descriptions were made independent of and prior to the theory we're testing.
lines.zh: “这些描述独立于我们正在测试的理论，并且先于我们正在测试的理论。
cloze: "These
were made independent of and prior to the theory we're testing.

lines.t: In future, if social scientists are serious about testing theories of morality, they will need to gather new data, more systematically, out in the field."
lines.zh: 未来，如果社会科学家认真地检验道德理论，他们将需要在现场更系统地收集新数据。”

lines.t: When it comes to food, color is money.
lines.zh: 对于食物来说，颜色就是金钱。
cloze: When it comes to food,
is money.

lines.t: Food companies know that better color gives better prices, so they ensure that their products are attractive in color to bolster earnings.
lines.zh: 食品公司知道更好的颜色可以带来更好的价格，因此他们确保其产品在颜色上具有吸引力以增加收入。

lines.t: Oranges, for example, have to meet specific color standards.
lines.zh: 例如，橙子必须满足特定的颜色标准。
cloze: Oranges, for example, have to meet
color standards.

lines.t: And oranges are just the beginning.
lines.zh: 橙子只是一个开始。

lines.t: There are color standards for foods including French fries, tomatoes, pumpkins, olives, honey and cherries.
lines.zh: 炸薯条、西红柿、南瓜、橄榄、蜂蜜和樱桃等食品都有颜色标准。
cloze: There are color standards for foods
French fries, tomatoes, pumpkins, olives, honey and cherries.

lines.t: The attention to color is for good reason.
lines.zh: 对颜色的关注是有充分理由的。

lines.t: For all the talk of the tongue, our eyes really might be the most important part of the eating experience.
lines.zh: 对于所有的舌头谈话来说，我们的眼睛确实可能是饮食体验中最重要的部分。
cloze: For all the talk of the tongue, our eyes really might be the most important part of the eating

lines.t: A great number of our brain functions are dedicated to processing vision, while only a percent or two is given over to taste faculties, and the result is that color actually changes how we taste food.
lines.zh: 我们的大量大脑功能专门用于处理视觉，而只有百分之一或百分之二的功能用于味觉功能，其结果是颜色实际上改变了我们品尝食物的方式。

lines.t: Scientists have demonstrated many times the importance of color to taste.
lines.zh: 科学家多次证明了颜色对味道的重要性。
cloze: Scientists have demonstrated many times the
of color to taste.

lines.t: In a 1980s study, for example, test participants were asked to name the flavor of the beverage they were drinking without being able to see that beverage.
lines.zh: 例如，在 20 世纪 80 年代的一项研究中，测试参与者被要求说出他们正在喝的饮料的味道，而无法看到该饮料。

lines.t: Only one in five was able to identify it as orange.
lines.zh: 只有五分之一的人能够识别出它是橙色的。
cloze: Only one in five was able to
it as orange.

lines.t: But when they were allowed to see what they were drinking which was orange in color, each of them identified the orange flavor.
lines.zh: 但当他们看到自己喝的橙色液体时，每个人都辨认出了橙色的味道。

lines.t: And when a drink that was lime flavor was colored orange, nearly half of respondents identified the flavor of the beverage as orange.
lines.zh: 当酸橙味饮料变成橙色时，近一半的受访者认为该饮料的味道是橙色。
cloze: And when a drink that was lime flavor was colored orange, nearly half of
identified the flavor of the beverage as orange.

lines.t: None made that mistake when the beverage was green in color.
lines.zh: 当饮料是绿色时，没有人犯这个错误。

lines.t: What's happening when someone fails to identify the flavor of a beverage they can't see or that has an abnormal color?
lines.zh: 当有人无法识别他们看不到的饮料的味道或颜色异常时，会发生什么？
cloze: What's happening when someone fails to identify the flavor of a

lines.t: Is it that participants can't discern what the flavor is, and so rely on visual cues?

lines.t: Or does color actually change the experience of taste?

of taste?

lines.t: The key to these questions is the effect of color on expectation.
lines.zh: 这些问题的关键是颜色对期望的影响。

lines.t: The brain makes predictions using color.
lines.zh: 大脑利用颜色进行预测。

lines.t: These predictions rely on expectations that come from experience.
lines.zh: 这些预测依赖于来自经验的期望。

lines.t: Research shows that we're all born liking sweet things and desire to eat them, but we aren't born knowing what the sweet things we crave look like.
lines.zh: 研究表明，我们生来就喜欢甜食并渴望吃它们，但我们并不是生来就知道我们渴望的甜食是什么样的。
cloze: Research shows that we're all born liking sweet things and desire to eat them, but we aren't born
what the sweet things we crave look like.

lines.t: So we need to learn this over time.
lines.zh: 所以我们需要随着时间的推移来学习这一点。

lines.t: The brain gets information from the environment.
lines.zh: 大脑从环境中获取信息。

lines.t: And we learn, for example, that fruits go from green and sour to red and ripe and sweet.
lines.zh: 例如，我们了解到水果会从绿色、酸味变成红色、成熟、甜美。

lines.t: Thus, if we see a green berry, we equate its color with a sour taste, and just looking at a red fruit will activate our expectations that it will taste sweet and delicious.
lines.zh: 因此，如果我们看到绿色浆果，我们就会将其颜色等同于酸味，而仅仅看到红色水果就会激发我们对它味道香甜可口的期望。
